extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural community: grant applicants and peer reviewers for Research Project Grants (RPGs)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes NIH's simplified peer review framework for Research Project Grant applications (RPGs), reorganizing the traditional five review criteria into three factors to focus reviewers on whether proposed research can and should be conducted. Includes how each factor is scored and how they inform the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central review question: 'Can and should the proposed research project be conducted?'
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplified framework focuses peer reviewers on the key question needed to assess the scientific and technical merit of proposed research projects: 'Can and should the proposed research project be conducted?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing directs reviewers to concentrate on whether the project is both doable (feasible, rigorous) and worth doing (important, innovative), and serves as the overarching lens for assessing scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (Significance and Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 1 combines Significance and Innovation and is scored on a factor score of 1–9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate how important the research question is and whether the project advances new concepts or approaches (significance and innovation). This factor receives a numeric score (1 = best to 9 = worst) to reflect importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 2 corresponds to Approach and is scored on a factor score of 1–9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess the scientific rigor of the proposed methods and the feasibility of completing the work as proposed. This factor is given a numeric score (1–9) reflecting quality of the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (Investigator and Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 3 combines Investigator and Environment and is rated as either 'sufficient for the proposed research' or 'not sufficient' (if not sufficient, reviewers must provide an explanation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project team and institutional environment provide the expertise, personnel, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed work. Unlike Factors 1 and 2, Factor 3 is a binary sufficiency determination with required explanation if judged insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact score (integration of all three factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider all three factors in determining the overall impact score, which reflects their overall assessment of the likely impact of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score synthesizes judgments about Importance (Factor 1), Rigor/Feasibility (Factor 2), and Expertise/Resources (Factor 3). Reviewers use the three-factor assessments to arrive at a single overall impact judgment used in funding considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original five review criteria (Significance, Innovation, Approach, Investigator, Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior review structure comprised five criteria: Significance, Innovation, Approach, Investigator, and Environment (derived from NIH peer review regulations 42 C.F.R. Part 52h.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simplified framework reorganizes these five criteria into three broader factors (Factor 1 combines Significance & Innovation; Factor 2 is Approach; Factor 3 combines Investigator & Environment). This provides continuity with previous evaluative concepts while reducing the number of separate scored dimensions.
